title: Setting our sights on Wikimanía Santiago
content:
As the sun sets over the Seine and Wikipedia’s 25th year draws to a close, we set our sights on Santiago. Sitting at the foot of the Andes mountains – the largest mountain range on land spanning seven South American countries – the city embodies the cultural richness, diversity and dynamism of the region. 

The Wikimedia movement also faces unprecedented change. The open spirit that once defined the Internet is at an inflection point, under threat from increasing concentration in the hands of few, surveillance, geopolitical fragmentation, and changes to the technological landscape. Against this backdrop, Santiago offers a powerful setting for the Wikimedia movement to come together and respond to a fundamental question: What kind of Internet do we want?

title: One day to celebrate and reflect with Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia
content:
On 30 August 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, 27 community members were invited from across the country to attend the annual strategic meeting of Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia. As a programme manager for ESEAP Hub, I was invited to attend and had the privilege to learn from local leaders gathering from Sabah, Sarawak, and West Malaysian communities. I shared the vision of ESEAP Hub as a service provider for East Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific region. 

For ESEAP Hub, WCUGM’s role is instrumental in the establishment and implementation of Hub’s theory of change. Four Wikimedians from Malaysia take part as ESEAP Community Connector and drive the leadership as members of the Steering Committee. In the coming months, ESEAP Hub will collaborate with WCUGM in project partnership for training of trainers on AI, indigenous communities, and gender responsiveness within the ESEAP region. Our ongoing discussion to support Brunei Darussalam will also hopefully be realized by the end of the year.

title: Capturing Local Stories – Wiki Village Ganggyeong Project
content:
It sounds like a joke, but the weakest area on the Korean Wikipedia is Korea itself. At one point, the community even debated whether to fill the gap by translating Korea-related articles from the English Wikipedia. The reasons are tangled, but it comes down to a loop: the articles are in poor shape, so nobody wants to touch them; and because nobody touches them, they stay in poor shape. The Korean Wikipedia we have today is what that loop, left to roll on, has produced.

I expect everyone reading this is nodding along — yes, this is a problem, and some of you might have a similar problem on your Wikipedia. But how many of you would raise a hand and volunteer to sort it out yourself? And there is simply far too much of it for one or two people to take on. What is needed, then, is something that pushes people into going out, finding sources for themselves, and building Korea-related articles up.

The Wiki Village Project was created to be that something. We took our starting point from Japan’s Wikipedia Town, but where those events are led by local residents, we chose a form in which editors travel to the town instead.

title: WACANA Puts Self-determination at The Center of AI Literacy
content:
Published to mark International Literacy Day, 8 September 2026

This year marks the 60th International Literacy Day, under the theme “Literacy for people, the planet, and prosperity.” Sixty years on, literacy means more than reading and writing. It also means being able to question the information in front of us, understand the technologies shaping it, and decide on our own terms what role those technologies should play in our lives.

As Hardiansyah, Chair of the Executive Board of Wikimedia Indonesia, puts it:

“Literacy is not only about reading or writing; it is also about opening a window to the world. Through Wikimedia’s open knowledge movement, we can make knowledge freely available in Indonesian and in many other languages so that anyone can access it. This spirit of openness means that knowledge is not something held by only a few but a shared resource that everyone can benefit from.”

title: Reflections on Wikimania 2026: History and Lessons Learned
content:
Wikimania brings together Wikimedians from around the world to discuss challenges facing their projects, share achievements, and discover aspects of the Wikimedia movement they may not have encountered before. It is a large gathering that combines conference sessions, workshops, meetups, and many other activities. Wikimania 2026 took place in Paris, France, from July 21 to 25, 2026.

I received a scholarship to attend as part of the ESEAP delegation and traveled to Paris as one of five Korean participants.

I arrived in Paris on July 20 and spent the following day participating in the Users with Extended Rights Convening, part of the pre-conference program. Users with extended rights, or UwERs, include administrators, CheckUsers, bureaucrats, interface administrators, and others who hold permissions beyond those needed for ordinary reading and editing on Wikimedia projects. The gathering offered an opportunity to discuss shared challenges and exchange practical knowledge and experiences.

title: A Slovene in Armenia: The Best Wiki Experience of My Life
content:
In August 2026, as part of CEE Hub‘s Peer Learning Exchange, I travelled from Slovenia to Armenia to take part in the Summer WikiCamp, organised by Wikimedia Armenia and held in Tsaghkadzor. In my head, the plan behind the exchange was pretty straightforward: I would participate in WikiCamp activities, learn from the organisers, connect with people, spend some time there, and that’s it. But pretty quickly I realised it was going to be a completely different experience from what I had anticipated.

Let me start by saying that I have been to quite a few Wikimedia events by now. I have attended conferences, meetings, edit-a-thons, workshops, and Wikimania. I have met hundreds of people, worked on projects, given presentations, and spent countless hours talking about Wikipedia.

And yet… somehow, a WikiCamp in Armenia became the best Wikimedia experience of my life.

title: Dagbani Wikimedians Take Wikipedia Awareness to Radio, Promote Language Diversity Conference 2026
content:
The Dagbani Wikimedians User Group (DWUG) has stepped up its public awareness efforts to help more people understand Wikipedia, Wikimedia projects, and the role they can play in preserving and promoting Dagbani and other African languages online.

As part of this effort, members of the user group participated in radio discussions on Zaa Radio 99.3 FM on 22 August 2026 and Dagbon FM 102.5 on 5 September 2026.

Representing the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group during the radio engagements were Abdul-Rafiu Fuseini (Alhaji Darajaati), Hamidu Rukaya (Ruky Wunpini), Fuseini Mugisu Suhuyini (Sir Amugi), and Musah Fuseini (Musahfm). 

The radio engagements provided an opportunity to speak directly to listeners about the work of Wikimedians, the importance of contributing knowledge to Wikimedia projects, and the growing presence of Dagbani in the digital space.

One of the main areas discussed during the interviews was the difference between Wikipedia, Wikimedia, and Wikimedians.

title: Colours of Celebration: The Winners of Wiki Loves Bangla 2026
content:
Hundreds of people sit in long, orderly rows at Masjid Al Mustafa in Dhaka, waiting to break their fast during Ramadan. Seen from above, the gathering takes on an almost geometric form: parallel lines of worshippers and shared tables fill the mosque’s illuminated centre, framed by the sweeping curves of its architecture and the darkness beyond.

The photograph, taken by Rakibul Alam Khan, is the winner of Wiki Loves Bangla 2026. It captures a familiar communal tradition from an unexpected perspective, bringing together faith, shared experience and visual symmetry in a single frame. The orderly gathering is not only a record of iftar, but also a reflection of how festivals and observances bring communities together—an idea that runs throughout this year’s winning photographs.

The jury was particularly drawn to the relationship between the congregation and the architecture surrounding it. Biswarup Ganguly highlighted how the parallel rows of people complement the symmetry of the setting, while Abdul Momin praised the architectural framing and composition, though he noted that the large dark areas around the gathering slightly weaken the overall visual balance.

title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 37
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Updates for editors

  • Add a Link has been upgraded for English Wikipedia users with improved detection of links that have different capitalization. This will help reduce ambiguous suggestions caused by differences in capitalization in article titles, including articles about cultural goods. A second phase of improvements is planned, which will also prepare the feature for release in other languages. [1] [2]
  • The Article guidance feature will be enabled by default for junior editors on Simple English and Turkish Wikipedia starting 10 September 2026 following an experiment. Junior editors with 0 to 99 edits will automatically see the feature when they click a red link or use the “Madde oluşturto” option on Turkish Wikipedia to create a new article. The change is intended to help junior editors create higher-quality articles that meet each Wikipedia’s standards. Additional improvements will continue based on the experiment results and community feedback.

title: Meet Us in Accra: Language Diversity Conference 2026
content:
What happens when people who are working to promote, preserve, and develop different languages come together?

They share experiences, learn from one another, discuss the challenges they face, and look for practical ways to strengthen their communities.

That is what the Language Diversity Conference 2026 is about.

From 2 to 4 October 2026, Accra, Ghana, will host the inaugural Language Diversity Conference under the theme

“Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Knowledge Movement.”

The conference will bring together language activists, Wikimedia contributors, researchers, educators, community organizers, and others working to ensure that languages that are often underrepresented online have a place in the digital world.

Language is not only about communication. It carries our history, culture, traditions, and knowledge. Yet many Indigenous and minoritised languages still have limited representation on the internet. This makes it important for language communities to take an active role in documenting their languages and making knowledge available in them.

title: A different way to find common ground
content:
An adaptation of Polis for the Wikimedia ecosystem, currently a live prototype. This post continues after ‘We need to innovate with Wikimedia decision-making‘. This prototype is part of the Next25 initiative attempt to arrive at more constructive attitude towards decision making.

We have a lot of decisions to make in the next year in our movement. As the number of visitors to Wikipedia is dropping, the internet around us is changing rapidly. This means that as a movement, we will have some hard decisions to make where we go. As WMF Executive Director Bernadette Meehan summarized: we need to evolve, but in ways that strengthen our mission. 

As I laid out in my last post, we need better processes to make decisions than the Request for Comments. This is true for deciding on our outdated policies in our many communities (how do we welcome new contributors, how do we handle AI, what is the bureaucracy that we can handle as a less-active community?) and on directions for our movement (what should be our priorities? Are there opportunities for new projects? What technology should we develop, and what should it look like?).

title: From Armenia to Tunisia: The Story of Wikipedia Camp Tunisia 2026
content:
From 23 to 27 August 2026, Wikimedia Tunisia User Group, in partnership with the Association of Culture and Science in Metlaoui, organized Wikipedia Camp Tunisia 2026 at the Camping and Holiday Center in Bkalta, Tunisia.

The camp was the realization of a dream that had been growing within the Tunisian Wikimedia community for several years. Its main inspiration came from the successful WikiCamp Armenia, a pioneering project that brought Wikimedia contributors together through learning, collaboration, and community-building activities. The Armenian experience demonstrated how a camp could create a strong environment for both newcomers and experienced Wikimedians to learn from one another and contribute together.

Inspired by this model, Wikimedia Tunisia began developing the idea of creating a similar experience in Tunisia.

The camp was developed in cooperation with the Scouts of Tunisia. Before the camp, a series of workshops was organized for young participants from different Scout groups. These workshops introduced participants to Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects and encouraged them to discover how they could contribute to free knowledge.

title: Trails of Eastern Flavors and Culture: The Thrill of Cross-Project Contributions at the WikiRempah Meetup
content:
Meetups (Kopdar) are always highly anticipated moments for Wikimedia volunteers. Aside from being a space to connect, meetups often spark extraordinary collaborations. Not too long ago, I had the opportunity to participate in a very unique meetup event titled WikiRempah in Bandung, West Java, Indonesia on Sunday, August 9, 2026.

True to its name, this event highlighted the richness of spices and culture, but with an interesting cross-cultural twist: we documented the culinary and cultural heritage of Eastern Indonesia, yet channeled it into Sundanese-language Wikimedia projects and other global platforms. This activity was not just about editing; it was a contribution marathon involving four Wikimedia projects simultaneously.

The first session, which was highly memorable for me, was culinary documentation. Eastern Indonesian cuisine, famous for its rich herbs and spices, was the main star. We went to an authentic Eastern Indonesian restaurant, photographed, and documented these signature dishes, then uploaded the best visuals to the Wikimedia Commons repository so they could be freely used by anyone. One example I uploaded was a photo of a Ayam Woku Khas Sulawesi.

content:
• Wikidata MCP Server

    • 2026. Aug. 9th (Saturday)

    Under the storm of Typhoon Dolphin, COSCUP 2026 commenced, bringing partners from around the world together to celebrate the value of open technology. The Conference for Open Source Coders, Users & Promoters (COSCUP) is one of the biggest open source events in Taiwan. This year, one topic dominated the community: Artificial Intelligence, or Agent in the concurrent stage.

    This year, our joint track of Wikidata and OpenStreetMap not only showcased how our respective platforms contribute to the open community, but also explored how open data and open technology can support the rapidly developing world of artificial intelligence.

    One highlight was our presentation with our partner from Wikimedia Deutschland, focusing on the Wikidata MCP Server and the Wikidata Embedding Project.

    Artificial Intelligence has come to the stage like a storm and quickly become one of the most discussed technologies across every industry. No matter which side of the fence you are on, one thing is the same: we want to know more about it and how it may affect our lives.
